$comment: The risk tier of a diff, keyed by the trigger headings of .claude/skills/pr-review/checklist.md. Checked by scripts/check-review-tiers.mjs (npm run check:review-tiers; CI runs it), which fails BOTH on a heading with no row and on a row naming a heading that no longer exists -- the bidirectional shape check:root-scripts uses. This file is a declared copy of those headings, kept honest by that gate rather than by a comment. Spec: docs/specs/tiered-pr-review.spec.md (WS2, barwise-1037). Consumers read it through scripts/lib/review-tiers.mjs; two parsers over one table is the copy the rule forbids.

tiers.always: Applies to every pull request; not a path trigger.
tiers.high-risk: Liability concentrates here -- rework across downstream packages, or external harm through a shipped surface. WS4 blocks merge on these.
tiers.routine: CI and the ratchets carry it. No blocking review.
tiers.not-path-derivable: The checklist trigger is semantic, not path-shaped. The classifier CANNOT detect it, and saying so is the point: these stay with the deep review, and a row exists so the completeness gate still accounts for the heading.

trivial.why: A pull request is trivial only if EVERY changed file is under one of these, and a trivial PR gets no Copilot review (.github/workflows/copilot-review.yml). Measured over the last 60 merged PRs: 11 (18%) touched only .beads/issues.jsonl -- every one a one-file tracker closure -- and nothing else was plausibly trivial. Documentation is deliberately NOT here: PR #532 was docs-and-tracker only and a Copilot review found five real defects in it, the worst a spec diagram describing an implementation that no longer existed. Widen this list only with the same kind of evidence, because a wrong entry is a defect nobody looks at.

rows.heading: Every PR
rows.why: the group with no trigger -- spec named, tracking issue open, numbers carry commands, session review present

rows.heading: When a surface changed (CLI, MCP, VS Code)
rows.why: external harm: these are what ships to users, and the capability matrix goes stale silently

rows.heading: When `@barwise/core` changed
rows.why: rework: eleven downstream packages absorb a bad decision here (root CLAUDE.md). src/ and the exports map, not the whole package -- a change to core's own tests is the tests row, and measured over the last 40 merged PRs the wider glob made 4 of 13 core triggers reach nothing under src/ (tests, core's CLAUDE.md, mutation configs). The package.json half has fired 0 times in that window and is reasoning rather than measurement

rows.heading: When a type was introduced, or a field's type chosen
rows.why: triggers on what a hunk does, not where it lives; any .ts file can introduce a type

rows.heading: When a module, function, or interface was introduced, or a signature widened
rows.why: same shape: a widened signature is invisible to a path matcher

rows.heading: When a copy was added or a copy was edited
rows.why: a must-agree copy is a relation between two files, which no single-path glob expresses

rows.heading: When generated output changed
rows.why: drift tests already fail when output disagrees with its regenerator

rows.heading: When tests changed
rows.why: coverage thresholds and the mutation pass carry weakening; the deep review still runs its failure-mode checks

rows.heading: When a check, gate, hook, or script was added or changed
rows.why: this is the verification apparatus itself; a gate that stops answering is the failure this repo keeps finding (barwise-906, six occurrences)

rows.heading: When a spec was added or revised
rows.why: audit:specs guards the Status claim; the rest is judgment the deep review applies

rows.heading: When Python was touched
rows.why: dev-time only and never a runtime dependency (root CLAUDE.md); check:python-uv holds the lockfile discipline

rows.heading: When a skill, agent brief, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or prompt artifact changed
rows.why: instructions are logic: a rule change is a behaviour change with no test, and nothing else reviews it. The per-package CLAUDE.md files are named explicitly because `CLAUDE.md` is an exact path that matches only the root one -- 8 of the 13 package instruction files reached this row through no glob at all, and the other 5 only incidentally, via the surface or Python rows (WS3)

rows.heading: When a dependency was added
rows.why: external harm, supply-chain shaped. The LOCKFILES, not the manifests: a dependency change is always written into the lock by npm install or uv lock, and CI rejects a lock that disagrees with its manifest -- while a manifest edit on its own is almost always an npm script. Measured (WS3): over the last 20 merged PRs the manifest globs fired 5 times and 4 were npm script additions with no lockfile change; over 40, 7 of 8. Still makes every dependabot PR blocking, roughly five a week.
